lessons.title: Listen and speak: greetings at home
lessons.objective: Greet people correctly in the morning, in the afternoon and at night, and answer a greeting.
lessons.course:
We greet people with the right words for the time of day.
In the morning we say: Good morning. In the afternoon we say: Good afternoon. At night, before we sleep, we say: Good night.
When someone greets us, we answer with the same words and a smile: Good morning, Mama!

support.title: Say with the adult
support.text:
Good morning, Papa!
Good afternoon, Auntie!
Good night, Mama!

lessons.model: Bih wakes up and sees her father. She says: “Good morning, Papa!” He answers: “Good morning, Bih!” In the evening, before bed, she says: “Good night, Mama!”
lessons.guided: The adult shows three drawings: the sun rising, the sun high in the sky, the moon. For each drawing, say the greeting together, then play it: one person greets, the other answers.
lessons.exercise: It is the morning. You see your grandmother. What do you say?
lessons.remediation: Use only two drawings first (sun and moon): Good morning, Good night. Add Good afternoon when the two are well known.
lessons.transfer: Tomorrow, greet each person at home with the right words for the time of day.

practice.prompt: Match each moment of the day with its greeting.
practice.answer: sunrise: Good morning; after lunch: Good afternoon; before bed: Good night.
practice.explanation: Each greeting goes with a time of day.

practice.prompt: Listen and say each greeting after the voice.
practice.listen: Good morning. Good afternoon. Good night.
practice.answer: Good morning. Good afternoon. Good night.
practice.explanation: Say the whole greeting, then smile.

practice.prompt: Your uncle says: “Good afternoon!” What do you answer?
practice.explanation: We answer with the same greeting.

lessons.title: Read: the sounds s, a, t, p
lessons.objective: Say and read the letter sounds s, a, t, p and blend them into short words.
lessons.course:
Each letter has a sound. s sounds like a snake: sss. a sounds like in apple. t sounds like a clock: t, t, t. p sounds like a puff of air: p, p.
We put the sounds together to read a word: s-a-t gives sat; p-a-t gives pat; t-a-p gives tap.

support.title: Read with the adult
support.text:
s  a  t  p
sat  pat  tap  at

lessons.model: The adult points to each letter and says its sound, then slides a finger under the word: “t… a… p… tap!” The tap at home gives water.
lessons.guided: Make the words with letter cards: put s, a, t in a row. Say each sound, then say them faster until you hear the word. Do the same with p-a-t and t-a-p.
lessons.exercise: Blend the sounds and read the word: t – a – p.
lessons.remediation: Say only two sounds first (a-t: at), then add one sound in front (s-at: sat).
lessons.transfer: Find something at home that starts with the sound p or s and say the sound.
lessons.materials: Letter cards s, a, t, p.

practice.prompt: Put the letters in order to make the word “pat”.
practice.explanation: We read from left to right.

practice.prompt: Which word do the sounds s – a – t make?
practice.explanation: s, then a, then t: sat.

practice.prompt: Listen and say the sounds after the voice, then the word.
practice.explanation: Say each sound, then blend them.

lessons.title: Write: strokes, curves and my name
lessons.objective: Draw straight strokes, curves, zigzags and waves from left to right, then copy one’s own name.
lessons.course:
Before writing letters, the hand learns lines. A stroke goes straight down. A curve goes round like a smile. A zigzag goes up and down like a roof. A wave goes like water.
We always write from left to right. Our name starts with a capital letter: Bih, Ayuk, Nfor.
lessons.model: The adult draws a row of zigzags slowly from left to right and says: “Up, down, up, down.” Then writes the child’s name in large letters with a capital letter at the start.
lessons.guided: Trace each line in the air with your arm, then in sand or on a slate, then with a pencil. Copy your name under the model, letter by letter.
lessons.exercise: Draw a row of waves from left to right, then copy your name.
lessons.answer: A row of waves drawn from left to right, and the name copied with a capital letter.
lessons.remediation: Trace the lines on a model with a finger first. Copy only the first letter of the name, then add one letter each day.
lessons.transfer: Write your name on a drawing you made at home.
lessons.materials: Slate or tray of sand, pencil, a card with the child’s name.

practice.prompt: Trace a zigzag like a roof, from left to right.
practice.answer: A zigzag that goes up and down, from left to right.
practice.explanation: Start on the left side of the page.

practice.prompt: Copy your name. Start with a capital letter.
practice.answer: The name copied with a capital letter at the start.
practice.explanation: A name always starts with a capital letter.

practice.prompt: Which way do we write?
practice.explanation: In English, we write and read from left to right.

lessons.title: Words for things at home: nouns, hi and hello
lessons.objective: Name things at home with common nouns and use hi and hello to greet a friend.
lessons.course:
A noun is a word for a person, an animal, a place or a thing. At home we find: a bed, a chair, a pot, a mat, a door.
We say hi or hello to greet a friend: Hello, Tabi! Hi, Enow!

support.title: Say with the adult
support.text:
bed  chair  pot  mat  door
Hello, Tabi!

lessons.model: The adult touches things in the room and names them: “This is a chair. This is a door. This is a pot.” Then greets a friend: “Hello, Ashu!”
lessons.guided: Play “touch and say”: the adult names a thing, the child touches it and repeats the noun. Then swap roles.
lessons.exercise: Name two things you can find in a kitchen.
lessons.answer: For example: a pot and a plate.
lessons.remediation: Work with three real objects only and say their names several times before adding new ones.
lessons.transfer: At home, name five things in your room and say them to an adult.
lessons.materials: Real objects from the home (a cup, a spoon, a mat).

practice.prompt: Match each thing with the room where we use it.
practice.answer: bed: bedroom; pot: kitchen; chair: parlour.
practice.explanation: Each thing has its place in the home.

practice.prompt: Complete the greeting.
practice.explanation: Hello and hi are used to greet a friend.

practice.prompt: Is “chair” a noun? Answer yes or no.
practice.explanation: A chair is a thing, so “chair” is a noun.

lessons.title: Sets of things at home
lessons.objective: Make sets of objects that go together and say why they go together.
lessons.course:
A set is a group of things that go together. A set of spoons. A set of cups. A set of red things.
We draw a ring around the things of the same set. A thing that does not belong stays outside the ring.
lessons.model: On the table there are three spoons, two cups and a plate. The adult puts a rope around the spoons: “This is a set of spoons.”
lessons.guided: Sort real objects from the kitchen into sets. Say the name of each set: a set of cups, a set of spoons.
lessons.exercise: Here are: a cup, a cup, a spoon, a cup. Which thing is not in the set of cups?
lessons.remediation: Sort only two kinds of objects at first (cups and spoons).
lessons.transfer: At home, help to put the plates in one set and the cups in another set.
lessons.materials: Cups, spoons, plates, a rope or a string to make a ring.

practice.prompt: Match each thing with its set.
practice.answer: mango: fruits; shirt: clothes; pot: kitchen things.
practice.explanation: Things that go together make a set.

practice.prompt: Which one does not belong in the set of fruits?
practice.explanation: A chair is not a fruit.

practice.prompt: Draw a ring around a set of three spoons.
practice.explanation: The ring shows the set.

lessons.title: Numbers 0 to 10: how many?
lessons.objective: Count objects up to 10 and match each quantity with its number.
lessons.course:
We count each object once: one, two, three… The last number we say tells how many.
Zero (0) means none: there is nothing.
5 stones: ● ● ● ● ●
lessons.model: The adult counts the plates on the shelf, touching each one: “One, two, three, four. There are 4 plates.”
lessons.guided: Count stones and put the right number card next to each group. Make a group of 0: an empty plate.
lessons.exercise: How many legs does a chair have?
lessons.remediation: Count up to 5 with objects you can touch, then go on to 10.
lessons.transfer: Count the people who eat with you tonight.
lessons.materials: Stones or bottle tops, number cards 0 to 10.

practice.prompt: Count: ● ● ● ● ● ● ●. How many?
practice.explanation: Touch each dot once: 7.

practice.prompt: Match each group with its number.
practice.explanation: Zero means none.

practice.prompt: Put the numbers in order from 0 to 5.
practice.explanation: Each number is one more.

lessons.title: Patterns with shapes
lessons.objective: Recognise circles, squares, triangles and rectangles and continue a pattern made with them.
lessons.course:
Four shapes: a circle is round. A square has 4 equal sides. A triangle has 3 sides. A rectangle has 4 sides, two long and two short.
A pattern repeats: circle, square, circle, square… What comes next? A circle.
lessons.model: The adult shows a mat with a pattern: triangle, circle, triangle, circle. “The pattern repeats. Next comes a triangle.”
lessons.guided: Cut shapes from cardboard. Make a pattern with two shapes, then ask someone to continue it.
lessons.exercise: Continue the pattern: circle, triangle, circle, triangle, …
lessons.remediation: Use patterns of two shapes of different colours before adding a third shape.
lessons.transfer: Find a pattern on a cloth or a basket at home.

practice.prompt: How many sides does a triangle have?
practice.explanation: A triangle has 3 sides.

practice.prompt: Put the shapes in order to repeat the pattern: square, circle, square, circle.
practice.explanation: The pattern repeats two shapes.

practice.prompt: Which shape is round?
practice.explanation: A circle has no corners.

lessons.title: Morning, afternoon, night
lessons.objective: Associate daily activities with the periods of the day and respect a simple schedule.
lessons.course:
A day has periods. In the morning we wake up, wash and go to school. In the afternoon we come back, eat and play. At night we eat supper and sleep.
Things happen in order: first we wash, then we eat breakfast.
lessons.model: The adult tells Bih’s day: “In the morning she fetches water. In the afternoon she does her homework. At night she sleeps.”
lessons.guided: Sort pictures of daily activities into three columns: morning, afternoon, night.
lessons.remediation: Use two periods only (day and night), then divide the day into morning and afternoon.
lessons.transfer: Tell an adult three things you do in the morning, in order.

practice.prompt: Match each activity with its period.
practice.answer: waking up: morning; coming back: afternoon; sleeping: night.
practice.explanation: Each activity has its time.

practice.prompt: Put Bih’s morning in order.
practice.answer: wakes up, washes, eats breakfast, goes to school.
practice.explanation: Things happen one after the other.

practice.prompt: When do we eat breakfast?
practice.explanation: Breakfast is the first meal of the day.

lessons.title: My body and keeping it clean
lessons.objective: Name the main parts of the body and say how to keep each one clean every day.
lessons.course:
Our body has many parts: the head, the hair, the eyes, the ears, the nose, the mouth, the arms, the hands, the legs and the feet.
We keep our body clean every day: we bathe with soap and water, we brush our teeth, we comb our hair, we cut our nails and we wear clean clothes.
lessons.model: Before school, Bih bathes with soap, brushes her teeth, combs her hair and puts on a clean uniform. She is ready and fresh.
lessons.guided: Touch each part of your body when the adult names it. Then mime how you clean it: wash, brush, comb.
lessons.exercise: What do we use to brush our teeth?
lessons.remediation: Work with five parts only (head, eyes, mouth, hands, feet), then add the others.
lessons.transfer: Tonight, show an adult how you wash your hands and your feet.
lessons.materials: Soap, a towel, a toothbrush, a comb, a drawing of the body.

practice.prompt: Match each part of the body with what we use to clean it.
practice.answer: teeth: toothbrush; hair: comb; hands: soap and water.
practice.explanation: Each part of the body needs its own care.

practice.prompt: How often should we bathe?
practice.explanation: We bathe every day to stay clean and healthy.

practice.prompt: Name three parts of your face.
practice.answer: For example: the eyes, the nose and the mouth.
practice.explanation: The face has the eyes, the nose, the mouth, the cheeks and the forehead.

lessons.title: Bonjour, au revoir, merci
lessons.objective: Saluer poliment, prendre congé et remercier en français.
lessons.course:
En français, on dit « Bonjour » le matin et la journée (Good morning / Hello), « Bonsoir » le soir (Good evening).
Pour partir, on dit « Au revoir » (Goodbye) ou « À demain » (See you tomorrow).
On dit « Merci » (Thank you) quand on reçoit quelque chose.

support.title: Dis avec l’adulte
support.text:
Bonjour, maman !
Au revoir, papa !
Merci !

lessons.model: Le matin, Ayuk arrive à l’école et dit : « Bonjour, madame ! » Le soir, il dit : « Au revoir, madame ! À demain ! »
lessons.guided: Joue avec une marionnette : elle arrive, on dit « Bonjour » ; elle part, on dit « Au revoir ». Elle donne un fruit, on dit « Merci ».
lessons.exercise: Tu arrives à l’école le matin. Que dis-tu à la maîtresse ?
lessons.remediation: Travaille d’abord « Bonjour » et « Au revoir » avec des gestes (main qui salue).
lessons.transfer: Dis « Bonjour » et « Au revoir » en français à une personne de la maison.

practice.prompt: Relie chaque moment à la bonne formule.
practice.answer: arriver : Bonjour ; partir : Au revoir ; recevoir : Merci.
practice.explanation: Chaque moment a sa formule de politesse.

practice.prompt: Écoute et répète.
practice.explanation: Dis les mots avec un sourire.

practice.prompt: Quel mot dit-on pour remercier ?
practice.explanation: « Merci » veut dire thank you.

lessons.title: Rules at home
lessons.objective: Discuss the rules of the home and apply them in daily life.
lessons.course:
Every home has rules. We greet the elders. We help with small tasks. We keep our things tidy. We ask before we take something. We come home on time.
Rules help everybody to live together in peace.
lessons.model: At Ashu’s house, the rule is: after eating, each child takes his plate to the kitchen. Ashu does it without being told.
lessons.guided: Make a list of three home rules with the family. Draw one rule and say why it is important.
lessons.exercise: Say one rule of your home.
lessons.answer: For example: we greet the elders; we keep our things tidy.
lessons.remediation: Start with one rule that the child already follows and praise it.
lessons.transfer: Follow one home rule every day this week.

practice.prompt: Which one is a good home rule?
practice.explanation: Greeting the elders shows respect.

practice.prompt: Why do we have rules at home?
practice.answer: To live together in peace and help each other.
practice.explanation: Rules help everybody in the family.

practice.prompt: Match each situation with the right action.
pairs: take your plate to the kitchen
You want a toy of your brother.
practice.answer: plate to the kitchen; ask first; greet.
practice.explanation: Good actions follow the home rules.

lessons.title: Materials for crafts at home
lessons.objective: Identify natural, found and recyclable materials used for crafts, and follow good environmental rules.
lessons.course:
We can make things with many materials. Natural materials come from nature: leaves, seeds, sticks, clay. Found and recyclable materials are things people throw away: bottle tops, old newspapers, cartons, plastic bottles.
We collect clean materials and we never take dirty or sharp things.
lessons.model: Bih collects bottle tops, a carton and some dry leaves. She will use them to make a picture.
lessons.guided: Collect five clean materials around the house. Sort them: natural or recyclable.
lessons.exercise: Name one natural material we can use for crafts.
lessons.answer: For example: leaves, seeds, sticks or clay.
lessons.remediation: Sort only two kinds: things from nature and things from the dustbin (clean).
lessons.transfer: Keep a box at home for clean recyclable materials.
lessons.materials: Clean bottle tops, cartons, dry leaves, seeds, a box.

practice.prompt: Match each material with its group.
practice.answer: leaves: natural; bottle tops: recyclable; clay: natural.
practice.explanation: Natural materials come from nature.

practice.prompt: Which material should we NOT collect?
practice.explanation: Broken glass can cut us.

practice.prompt: Draw two materials you collected.
practice.explanation: Draw and name each material.

lessons.title: Drawing my house with shapes
lessons.objective: Draw plain shapes and use them to draw a house; colour it with appropriate colours.
lessons.course:
We can draw many things with simple shapes. A house: a square for the walls, a triangle for the roof, a rectangle for the door, small squares for the windows.
We colour slowly, without going out of the lines.
lessons.model: The adult draws a square, puts a triangle on top, then a rectangle at the bottom: “Here is a house.”
lessons.guided: Draw your house with shapes. Colour the roof, the walls and the door.
lessons.exercise: Which shape can be the roof of a house?
lessons.remediation: Trace the shapes on a model before drawing them alone.
lessons.transfer: Draw the house of a member of your family.
lessons.materials: Paper, pencil, coloured pencils or crayons.

practice.prompt: Draw a house with a square, a triangle and a rectangle.
practice.explanation: Square: walls; triangle: roof; rectangle: door.

practice.prompt: Match each part of the house with its shape.
practice.answer: roof: triangle; walls: square; door: rectangle.
practice.explanation: Shapes help us draw.

practice.prompt: How do we colour well?
practice.explanation: Careful colouring is beautiful.

lessons.title: Walking and balancing
lessons.objective: Walk in different ways and keep balance on one foot and on a line.
lessons.course:
We can walk fast, slowly, on tiptoe, on our heels, backwards. To keep balance, we look in front of us and open our arms.
We always warm up before and we drink water after.
lessons.model: The adult walks on a line drawn on the ground, arms open, looking straight ahead.
lessons.guided: Walk on a line, then stand on one foot and count to five. Change foot.
lessons.exercise: What helps us keep our balance?
lessons.answer: Looking in front and opening our arms.
accept: Looking in front and opening our arms
lessons.remediation: Hold the adult’s hand on the line first.
lessons.transfer: Play “walk on the line” with your brothers and sisters.
lessons.materials: Chalk or a rope on the ground, an open space.

practice.prompt: Stand on one foot and count to five. Which number do you stop at?
practice.explanation: One, two, three, four, five: then change foot.

practice.prompt: Match each walk with how we do it.
pairs: on the front of the feet
on the back of the feet
practice.answer: tiptoe: front; heels: back; backwards: going back.
practice.explanation: There are many ways to walk.

practice.prompt: What do we do before exercise?
practice.explanation: Warming up prepares the body.

lessons.title: My language and the languages around me
lessons.objective: Name the language of the family and recognise that many languages are spoken in the community.
lessons.course:
Cameroon has many national languages. Each family has its language, for example Bassa, Ewondo, Duala, Fulfulde, Mungaka, Bakweri or Kom. English and French are the official languages.
We are proud of our language and we respect the languages of others.
lessons.model: Ayuk says: “At home we speak Kenyang. My friend Bih speaks Lamnso. At school we speak English.”
lessons.guided: Ask an adult at home: “What is our language?” Then find out the language of two friends.
lessons.exercise: What is the language of your family?
lessons.answer: The child names the family language.
lessons.remediation: Start with the language of one person the child knows well (a grandparent).
lessons.transfer: Learn to say “hello” in the language of a friend.
lessons.materials: Klassia’s “Home language” page to record family words, if the family wishes.

practice.prompt: Which ones are the official languages of Cameroon?
practice.explanation: Cameroon has two official languages and many national languages.

practice.prompt: Ask your family how to say “hello” in your language. Say it aloud.
practice.answer: The word for “hello” in the family language.
practice.explanation: Every language has its greetings.

practice.prompt: Name one language spoken by a friend or a neighbour.
practice.answer: For example: Bassa, Duala, Fulfulde, Mungaka.
practice.explanation: Many languages live together in Cameroon.

competencies: Listening and Speaking: generalities, my language

lessons.title: Devices at home: radio, television, phone
lessons.objective: Identify common ICT devices at home and say what they are used for.
lessons.course:
ICT devices help us to receive and send information. At home we can find a radio (we listen), a television (we watch and listen), a phone (we call and send messages), sometimes a computer.
We use them with an adult and we take care of them.
lessons.model: In the evening, the family listens to the news on the radio. Papa calls Grandma on the phone.
lessons.guided: Look around the house and find the ICT devices. Say what each one does.
lessons.exercise: Which device do we use to call someone?
lessons.remediation: Use pictures of three devices first.
lessons.transfer: Watch or listen to a children’s programme with an adult.
lessons.materials: Pictures of ICT devices; the devices of the house (with an adult).

practice.prompt: Match each device with what it does.
practice.answer: radio: listen; television: watch and listen; phone: call.
practice.explanation: Each device has its use.

practice.prompt: Which one is an ICT device?
practice.explanation: A radio receives information.

practice.prompt: With whom do we use devices?
practice.explanation: An adult helps us use devices safely.
